caption: Exploration 01 overview: four concepts, research, comparison and recommendation.
A · System Atlas: whole-system map. Solid land = decided, hatched = suspected, fog = unexplored. Legend lists the three places needing judgement.
A · Zoomed into Actions; the evidence drawer asks whether three blue buttons are one job, with specimens, screens, observed/suspected facts and options.
A · Preview before confirming: name the role and see what changes; affected roads animate on the map.
A · After three decisions: fog lifted, Primary action flagged as decided, Business themed, Book now marked as an exception. Survey log at the bottom allows undo.
B · Design Dialogue: today’s briefing. First question (one red used for errors and deals) with evidence; the emerging system on the right.
B · After answering: the system replies with what changed and the codex gains Danger and Promotion tiles. Undo inline.
B · Blue buttons question with the overlay view and the “push back” panel open (pre-written challenges or free text).
B · “Same job, except…”: the designer taps the button that doesn’t belong before confirming.
B · Follow-up question raised by the previous answer, previewing the Business portal in a partner’s brand colour.
B · Briefing complete: what changed, what remains uncertain, and the updated codex.
C · Living System: concepts as membranes of grains (each ≈25 elements). Teal = decided, amber dashed = suspected, pink = anomaly.
C · Red selected: inspector shows evidence and a split preview; ghost targets show where grains will go.
C · Dragging Business onto Primary action asks what “identical” means: theme it, merge it, or leave apart.
C · After decisions: Danger and Promotion split, Primary action confirmed, Business themed, Book now pinned as exception. History strip at the bottom.
C · “By appearance” lens: grains regroup by look; glowing grains look alike but mean different things.
C · Scrubbing history back to an earlier state, with “Continue from here” or “Back to latest”.
D · System Review: status strip, ranked review list, and a proposal with the inventory wall of screenshots as evidence.
D · The proposed component as a Figma-style variant sheet, adjustable before approving with changes.
D · Business proposal shown as variable modes; “Ask someone” delegates to the owner.
D · Library tab after decisions: status labels show Live, Waiting and Needs review.
D · Decision records with reasons, evidence and Reopen.
Exploration 02 overview: shared scenario, three prototypes, comparison and patterns.
A · Library-first: the Primary action page. Two dashed cards next to Default are product uses the library doesn’t describe yet.
A · Checkout card expanded in place: comparison, difference, context, question, suggested answer, and the “Not quite” alternatives.
A · After both decisions: Large is a variant, Checkout is an exception, properties, usage and “Why it looks like this” all updated.
A · Changing an earlier decision reopens the same panel with the current answer highlighted.
B · Decision-first: the component as it is today, and a single prompt to look at the first change.
B · One question with evidence at the scale of the difference (magnified corners), the most likely answer first and “Why?” expanded.
B · “That’s not right” reveals other readings so the designer can correct the assistant.
B · Result: what was decided, whether the product changes, and the updated component card.
B · Second question: Search height shown with measured rulers.
B · Library view: variants and exceptions, each change with Revisit.
C · Workbench: the component as places a finding can go (left) and a short introduction (right).
C · Checkout finding on the right; places on the left, one marked as the assistant’s suggestion.
C · Choosing a different place previews it live in the library with consequences, noting it overrides the suggestion.
C · Both placed. Selecting the Checkout item shows its reasoning and lets you move it or take it out.
